results.caption:
The Best Running Gear in 2026 (in my opinion)

#running #runner #marathon #marathontraining #recommendations
results.profileBio:
I love running and making videos about running
@bpnsupps athlete
results.transcript: This is all the best running gear you can buy in 2026. So many different brands make great running gear, but here are the things I actually use and recommend as a runner. All right, sunglasses. I recommend the Oakley Radar EVs. These look awesome. They're super comfortable and they don't bounce when you're running. I also recommend the Oakley eye jackets. Same thing. They fit super comfortable on your face. A more affordable option that looks similar are the Rendezvous R3s. Good running headphones are super important to me. The Beats Powerbeats Pro 2s have the all-around best fit and sound quality. I've also been loving the Shox Open Dots. Not quite as good sound quality, but still really good. The Shox Open Run Pro 2s are great if you want to feel more aware and have more of an open ear feel. The DSG Quarter Crew socks have and probably always will be my favorite running socks. Then in second place come the Nike Unicorn socks. All right, now the fun stuff, shoes. I have tested all of these extensively. Here are my recommendations. For an affordable daily trainer, New Balance Ellipse. Another well-priced daily trainer are the Adidas Evo SL. My favorite daily trainer to date are the Nike Vomero Plus. For race day or workout shoes, Nike Alpha Fly 3s, Hoka CLO 3s, Adidas Adios Pro 4s, which are probably my favorite race day shoes. And then finally, Saucony Endorphin Elite 3s. If you're a shorts person, my favorite are the Satisfy Spaceo shorts, but they're really expensive. A more affordable option are the New Balance RC shorts. Lululemon Fast and Free shorts are good. And then of course, Nike Trail. I mostly wear half tights. The ones I recommend most are the Lululemon Fast and Free. These will genuinely change your life. Pretty much every brand makes a good running shirt. Just make sure it's lightweight and breathable. My favorite shirts are definitely Satisfy, but they're very expensive. If you're feeling bold, the Nike Radical Airflow shirt is pretty crazy. The two hats I recommend are the CLA hats and the Aloe hats. The CLA 5 panel hat is very flexible and comfortable. And same thing with the Aloe Performance hat. I love this thing. The watch I use is the Garmin 4Runner 970. If you want a more affordable option, use the Coro Space Pro. I wear the Whoop 5.0. I can't sleep with my Garmin, but I can sleep with my Whoop, and it tracks everything I do 24-7. My most essential running supplements are BPN Go gels and BPN electrolytes. And then lastly, for recovery, I recommend the Norma Tech boots.

results.transcript: Every runner only needs to run by heart rate, is what I would say if I was a complete idiot. We need to stop comparing to answer this comment and turn heart rate off. It's giving people anxiety and the wrong thing that you need to focus on. We race for time and performance, not the lowest heart rate. So I'm going to talk about heart rate, when to look at it, when to not look at it, what I prescribe for my athletes, and what I've done after 22 marathons, 16 ultras, 2 full Ironman when it comes to my training. Number one for everyday running for beginners, you should care about pace and perceived effort. Your easy day. Can you talk? Can you sing a song? Can you feel like you can hold this for five hours? Threshold is very simple. You need to run at the prescribed pace and it is okay to fail workouts. Why do you go by pace and not heart rate? When it comes to that marathon, especially when you want to PR, you need to look at your pace. You're not going to say, I'm going to run at 145 beats per minute. No one says that. And most of the time people have their heart rate off and they just look at distance and pace. They have no external anxiety, no depression, et cetera. Why? Because heart rate can vary so many things. Obviously genetics play the number one role that people don't think about. Number two, heat, humidity. Then you have sleep, dehydration, et cetera. It could be 15 to 20 beats higher. Yet that perceived effort could feel great. You look at your watch and say, fuck, I'm going too fast. Let's slow down. You miss your PR. No. Okay. Then you need to look at your overall training zones. The only way that I recommend getting a max heart rate is going to get your VO2 and your threshold lactate tested. Your watch is going off an optical sensor, which is wrong about 80% of the time, especially if you have tattoos or et cetera. From there, you can dial in what your pace exactly needs to be. Or if you don't want to pay the $200, that's fine. Run a 5K. Look at your pace. You probably will get close to your max heart rate and dial it in from there. The other thing, when you look at heart rate, this is very important. I don't ignore heart rate all the time. I look at it month to month, three months, six months, and of course, a year. Every day it's going to vary. Okay. You're not going to see any changes when it comes to pacing or heart rate every day. But what about three months, six months? This is when you can look at your chart and start to compare within you. Stop comparing from... the external saying, oh my God, their heart rate's 135. No, my heart rate is a 135 at a 730, 740 beats per minute. When I started running, it was a 155 for an 830 pace. Okay. You look at that over the year because that shows you that you're getting fitter. Now, when to kind of tone down your training, you're going to be extremely fatigued. Your resting heart rate can be 10 to 20 beats higher, not just for one day over the course of seven to 10 days, because that's going to tell you something. Okay. Then you can look at HRV, not every single day over the course of a month to three months and dial in what you need to dial in. Other than that, guys, you need to train by pace and effort, especially for new runners or runners that are going, let's just say at the advanced level, they are going a lot of the times off of pace. Yes. Heart rate is good to look at here and there, but it's not the end all be all. I think we need to turn it off on our watch, run free, run off of pace, give yourself ample amount of time. What took me a year to lower my heart rate is going to take someone else two, three, four years, depending on how much volume, the level of fitness, obviously they're genetics. Other than that, I'm going to eat my breakfast. It's five o'clock in the morning. I hope this video helped drop your questions, comments. I'm out of here.
